title: Enable `git diff` for individual sections of the `source` file

labels.name: editorial
labels.description: Changes that do not affect how the standard is understood

body:
This has already been suggested back in 2018 with #3705, which was closed. However I find the discussion back then to be quite lacking, so I am opening a new issue for this, hoping to make a better case and to better address the various concerns.

Firstly a >140,000 line file is very obviously unnecessarily hard to edit. Even if you feel comfortable editing a hundred thousand line long file, having all the source in one file prevents the multipage HTML version from having a handy "Edit this page" link that directly takes you to the right source file in GitHub. Furthermore the file is so big that `git blame` takes a long time. GitHub's user interface also does not really support such long files, viewing the file shows  "Sorry about that, but we can’t show files that are this big right now." and attempting to use GitHub's blame feature just times out.

However what I find much more pressing is that with all the source in one file, people that implement some part of the specification cannot simply use the official repository with `git diff` to see what has changed in the specific part that is being implemented. For instance I am currently working on an HTML parser implementation and I'd like to be able to:

```
$ git diff $SOME_COMMIT src/parsing 
```

to see all the changes to the [parsing page](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html) since `$SOME_COMMIT`. But alas I currently can only diff the `source` file without being able to filter out what I don't care about.

Now we obviously do not want to loose the history of each line ... `git blame` should still report the same commits as before the split ... fortunately this is possible as described in [Keep git history when splitting a file](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3887736/keep-git-history-when-splitting-a-file).

The [html-build](https://github.com/whatwg/html-build) scripts would obviously need to be updated.
While existing PRs would need to be updated this could be automated using something like `git-filter-repo`.

What do you think about this?
